title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations (kv-batching + scheduling)
author: Priya Suresh
description: Motivation: upgrade the on-device attention kernels to FlashAttnV2 with fused rotary/rope ops and improved KV cache-friendly codepaths to reduce token-level latency and memory pressure for long-context workloads. This PR bundles four related areas: (1) replace legacy attention kernels with FlashAttnV2-backed implementations that support fused rotary/rope and mixed-precision paths; (2) introduce fused prepack/unpack ops to reduce memory copies in the fused-ops path; (3) KV-cache layout changes to enable continuous batching and async KV flushing with lower synchronization overhead; (4) scheduler heuristics to prefer low-latency paths for short requests while enabling higher throughput batching for background/async workloads. Changeset includes kernel dispatch, JIT kernel selection, unit tests, microbenchmarks, and rollout gating flags. Benchmarks: end-to-end 1.8x median token throughput for 8k-context models on A100-80GB with 16-token batch size, 20% median latency reduction for 2-32 token requests, and 12% lower peak GPU memory for 32k context experiments. Rollout plan: feature flag default off, staged rollout to dedicated pools, canary to internal perf canary pool, monitor token-latency and quality regressions via existing eval harness. Rollback: revert feature flag and the kernel selector; preserve old kernels during rollout for fast fallback. Related: ENG-2384 (kernel upgrade), ENG-2410 (kv batching), incident INT-5521 referenced for earlier regression investigation.

perf(attention): fused rotary/rope op implementation with mixed-precision support

changes_summary: Replaced legacy attention dispatch with flashattn_v2 dispatcher; implemented fused rotary/rope kernels with contiguous memory layout to eliminate intermediate copies; refactored KV cache to a contiguous chunked layout supporting async flush and continuous batching; added scheduler heuristics to route short requests to fast-path kernels and aggregate background requests for throughput. Added unit tests, microbenchmarks, and rollback flags.
